story: Archery Close takes its name from a cobbled dead-end street in London's Connaught Village, where its founders lived with their young daughters. Years later they moved to Stowe, Vermont, and opened a boutique on Mountain Road. It lists Barbour, Billy Reid, Dehen 1920, Marine Layer, Paul Smith and Wax London among its vendors. It is open every day, including Sunday afternoons.

story: Murray's Toggery Shop stands at the top of Main Street in Nantucket, where its own history page says R.H. Macy opened a dry goods store that became The Toggery Shop in 1843. Philip Murray bought it in 1945 and kept it open year round. His son Philip C. Murray introduced the canvas cloth that became Nantucket Reds in 1960 and in 1963 bought the Louis Coffin dry goods store next door, now the women's department. Patricia and John Murray, with Gilles Bridier, took over management in 1990, and the shop launched NantucketReds.com in 1996 as the island's first online store. It sells men's, women's and children's clothing, including its own Nantucket Reds label, Peter Millar, Barbour and Marine Layer.
